lead.title: ALK-Abelló: its Acarizax tablet succeeds in a Phase 3 in China against house dust mite allergy
lead.deck: In a randomized, double-blind trial of 327 participants (ages 12-65), Acarizax beat placebo by 1.11 points on the combined symptom-medication score (19.1% relative difference), well above the threshold agreed with Chinese authorities. ALK and partner GenSci aim to file in China in the first half of 2027, in a market of over 100 million people with dust mite allergy of whom fewer than one million receive immunotherapy.

milestone.title: Zealand: Kv1.3 blocker ZP9830 clears its multiple-dose phase with clean tolerability
milestone.summary: In 32 healthy volunteers dosed for four weeks, there were no serious or severe adverse events and no dose-limiting safety findings; pharmacokinetic data support longer trials. A Phase 1b trial with efficacy endpoints in plaque psoriasis has already started.
milestone.why: Kv1.3 is upregulated on effector memory T cells that sustain inflammation: the bet is to slow them while preserving the rest of the immune system. A Phase 2 in another autoimmune disease is planned for the first half of 2027 — a test of the approach beyond dermatology.

brefsEurope.title: CHMP recommends EU approval of Foundayo (orforglipron), Lilly's oral GLP-1
brefsEurope.summary: A once-daily non-peptide tablet for weight management and type 2 diabetes: weight loss of 5 to 11% at 72 weeks depending on dose (versus 2 to 2.5% on placebo). The European Commission now has to decide; it will compete with Novo's Wegovy pill, whose EU authorization was just granted.

brefsEurope.title: FDA approves Process 2.0 for SIMLANDI, Alvotech's Humira biosimilar
brefsEurope.summary: The new process more than doubles drug substance output per batch in the DSM2 suite in Reykjavik without changing upstream scale, freeing capacity for other products in the portfolio; it follows a recent approval of additional capacity at the same site.

brefsIntl.title: Lycia aims for a $228M IPO for its Xolair rival in food allergy
brefsIntl.summary: The planned IPO, reported by Fierce Biotech, would fund development of a candidate competing with omalizumab in food allergy: a market comparable for immunology platform valuations.

word.fr: Vector derived from a lentivirus to deliver a gene
word.definition: A disarmed virus from the lentivirus family, used as a vehicle to introduce a therapeutic gene into cells.

parts.label: Vector genome
parts.role: the payload: the therapeutic gene, without replication genes

parts.label: Production
parts.role: the packaging cells that make the particles

how.t: Producer cells assemble viral particles carrying the gene of interest, without the ability to replicate.
The particles infect the patient's cells (often collected then modified in the lab, as in CAR-T therapy).
The gene is delivered into the cell, which produces the missing protein or the desired receptor.

word.why: VC angle: lentiviral vectors are the bottleneck of ex vivo cell and gene therapy — manufacturing costs, production capacity and packaging-cell-free variants are investment theses in their own right, with seed to Series B tickets in Europe.
